pure-announcement.rationale: It is third-party news coverage of LangChain's argument about memory lock-in, not a launch, release note, or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept (proxy capture, MCP governance, SIEM gap, context layer, extensions, skills) covers agent-memory portability or harness lock-in.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The core claims are attributed to LangChain's published analysis and named individuals, though the 512,000-line Claude Code figure rests on unnamed leaked documentation.

durability.rationale: The three-level lock-in spectrum is a reusable framing, but this secondhand write-up leans on current product shapes (Responses API, Claude Managed Agents, Codex summaries) and a sloppy aggregator's retelling that even misdescribes LangChain as a blockchain company.

actionability.rationale: It tells a builder to weigh memory portability when picking a harness but offers no evaluation method beyond 'use the open-source alternative' the covered vendor sells.

atomicity.rationale: It carries one idea - memory flows through the harness, so proprietary harnesses convert accumulated memory into vendor lock-in, graded across three severity levels - statable in a single paragraph.
